title: Behavior
description: Schema for a behavior registry entry — a named physical law (e.g., conducts_current, has_resistance, produces_joule_heat). Per OBJECT-MODEL.md §6 + §15 deferred 'behavior registry shape'. Behaviors are registry-only (not instantiable) — they are referenced by devices' 'behaviors:' lists and by other behaviors' 'consequences:'. Behaviors have NO composition (they are abstract laws, not composed from lower-layer objects).

kind.description: Behaviors validate against this schema only — kind must be exactly 'behavior'.

layer.description: Behaviors live at the behavior layer.

parameters_required.description: Named slots the behavior needs from the object that adopts it. Each slot has a name, type, units (for quantity), allowed (for enum), and optional description. Empty array allowed for behaviors with no parameter inputs.

evaluates.description: Symbolic equation in human-readable math notation. The math at the meaning level — the validator engine reads this for documentation, and a future code registry (keyed by 'law') implements the actual evaluation. Optional: behaviors with solver_status of defined_not_solved or research_future may omit evaluates.

consequences.description: Behavior ids triggered as cascading consequences. For example: has_resistance produces produces_joule_heat. Empty array is legal (most behaviors have no cascading consequences).

law.description: Foreign key into a future code-implementation registry (e.g., 'ohm', 'joule', 'led_emission'). The validator engine in a later sprint will look up the implementation by this id. Optional: behaviors with solver_status of defined_not_solved or research_future may omit law.
